findings.text: the standing line is emitted only when the caller arms an interval: needs_remind_seconds is None unless remind is passed, and _needs_you_events returns on that condition before it yields anything (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2134-2137). No production caller passes remind: the only caller that reaches it with an interval is tests/test_follow_needs_you_line.py:127, and the crew follow --remind option (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3221) defaults to None, so every follower the fleet runs emits no needs-you line and no heartbeat. Plan section 7 asks for the opposite: emit the line after any transition that changes the set, and again on a cadence whether or not the set is empty, with the cadence defaulting to ten minutes. The section exists because a quiet pane must not look the same for a healthy follower and a dead one, and as landed it looks exactly the same. The worker disclosed this in follow_ons with the measurement behind it (unconditional emission measured 14 failed, 687 passed against the base arm's 3, every added failure in four frozen output contracts outside its write scope), so the repair is a coordinator ruling rather than a worker error: arm the line from the host/pane path, or relax the four frozen contracts. It blocks because the section cannot be called delivered while no follower shows the line the section was filed to add, and because the decision it needs is one the worker was fenced out of.

DEFAULT_REMIND_SECONDS = 600.0 is defined and never referenced anywhere in the repository, and its comment asserts what the plan asks for and the follower does not do (that the follower re-emits the line on this cadence). The plan's ten-minute default therefore survives only as dead code; either the emitter should read this constant as its default interval, or the constant should not sit here claiming a behaviour nothing runs.

the session-ownership filter at needs_you.py:142-145 and the bucket partition at needs_you.py:149-158 restate rules the repository already owns: _partition_session_rows (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:270) owns the rule that a pointer with no recorded owner stays in the counted set, and _fleet_counts (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:270 owns the rule that a pointer with no recorded owner stays in the counted set, and _fleet_counts (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1381-1419) owns the working/blocked/unpromoted partition including the held exclusion that needs_you.py:151 re-derives. The module's own docstring claims the counters cannot disagree with the line, and that holds only while two copies of the rule stay in step. The row list is a different output from the counts, so this is a partial reuse gap rather than a fork, which is why reuse scores 14 rather than below 5.

the parity assertion compares follow._needs_you_runs (tests/test_follow_needs_you_line.py:271) against need_module.needs_you_runs (:265), and reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:942 makes the former a one-line delegate of the latter, so the two sides move together and the assertion holds whatever either function does. It can redden only if a future edit re-forks the derivation and the fork diverges on this fixture, which is the contract worth guarding but is not the equality the case's own docstring claims. The rest of the case carries the durability weight: derived_nodes equals the set holding own-unpromoted, asserted against the fixture's literal node name, which is independent of the code.

the delivered manifest's tests: line is 'python -m pytest -q tests/test_follow_needs_you_line.py tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py (head tree, PYTHONPATH=<tree>/arms/head)' - a literal command with a description tail and an unsubstituted <tree> placeholder - and both baseline_suite.command and after_suite.command embed '<53 follower-touching files from ...>' and '<the same 53 files retargeted at arms/head2>', which the manifest contract refuses because a template command cannot be re-run. The gate receipt can fall back to each log's own '# command:' header (logs/head-needs-you.log line 4, logs/base-arm.log line 4), which carries the real command, but a reader parsing the manifest's own field gets prose and no runnable command.
